The newest results come first: [November 9](#nov9), on elliptic friction
contacts. The [sections after it](#pyramidal) are the November 8–9 runs on
MuJoCo's pyramidal contacts, kept for the record and marked as superseded.

Each clip replays calls that the planner actually made in its teacher runs
(branch `phase1/planar`). No motion here was staged for the
video. The search chose the edits (the contact changes), and each edit was
executed by the local solver the run used: the quasi-static realizer Λ_qs or
a learned skill Λ_RL (see [The local solver](../planar-build/local-solver.qmd)).
Each call was re-run in MJX from the logged start state, recorded, and
drawn. The re-run was checked against the log: the same success, the same
end formation, and the end pose within a few millimetres. One clip that did
not match is labelled **DIVERGED** below.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How to read a clip

- **View.** From the side, with +x to the **left**, as in the paper. The
  green surface is the platform, the grey one the floor, the blue ball the
  disk. A red stripe marks the face the box rests on at the start, so you
  can follow its rotation.
- **Top-left box.** The task and instance; the current segment *k/n* with its
  edit and formations (σ → σ′); the solver that ran it; the formation the
  recognizer reads right now, with **[TIE]** when two formations can't be
  told apart; and whether the re-run matched the log.
- **Speed.** Stated in the overlay at every moment. Λ_qs calls are about
  21 s long and mostly at rest, so they play at 3× while the box rests and
  in real time while it moves. The learned skills act in a fraction of a
  second, so their first 0.6 s plays at 0.25× (slow motion).
- **Cards.** A short hold after each segment, then the strict test's verdict
  (SOLVED, or FAILED with the clause that failed).
:::

## November 9: elliptic contacts, the redesign, and CMGMP {#nov9}

Three things happened on November 9. The simulator's friction model turned
out to be wrong for a box at rest, and was changed. A redesigned search
([Search](../planar-build/search.qmd#redesign)) solved its first lowering
tasks. And the CMGMP baseline was re-run on the new contacts. Tonight's work
fixed the lift's pivot; the redesign's full teacher run is starting now, so
its numbers are **pending**.

### The simulator, not the gate, was wrong

MuJoCo's default *pyramidal* friction cones let a box creep off a rest that
the statics say is held. *Elliptic* cones (impedance ratio 10), at the same
step and contact parameters, remove the creep. On the box leaning on the step
corner with the disk pulled away:

| | pyramidal (old default) | elliptic, impratio 10 (adopted) |
|---|---|---|
| creep, °/s | 0.40 | 0.008 |
| rests held for 10 s | 0 of 84 | 84 of 84 |
| simulator agrees with the gate (poses away from the tipping boundary) | 87 of 453 | 452 of 453 |

So the gate's statics were right; the simulator let held boxes slide. Every
scene now uses elliptic cones and full float32 matrix products, and every
result is being re-run on them. The results further down this page used the
pyramidal cones.

### CMGMP on elliptic contacts

CMGMP (the contact-mode-guided planner of Cheng et al., the authors' C++
code, patched for our disk's 1 N motors) ran on the 50 shared test starts,
25 per task. Each start gets up to 1,800 s; CMGMP is restarted with fresh
seeds until an executed plan passes. Every plan is executed in our MJX
simulator on elliptic contacts and graded by our strict test. A lift counts
only if the box ends *fully* on the platform, at rest.

| Task (25 starts) | within 60 s | within 300 s | within 1,800 s | plans claimed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| lift | 1 (1–20%) | 5 (9–39%) | 15 (41–77%) | 22 |
| lower | 14 (37–73%) | 21 (65–94%) | 24 (80–99%) | 25 |

95% Wilson intervals in brackets. Seeds run 0, 1, 2, …, so each budget's
column is a prefix of one run. The lift needs many restarts (median 141
planning attempts per start). An earlier grading of the same lift run used a
looser rule (the box only partly over the platform: 3 / 14 / 20) and is
superseded.

**Not yet a comparison.** Our planner has not run on these 50 starts. The
paired comparison (same starts, same goal test and grading, matched
wall-clock budget, McNemar's test) runs after the redesign's teacher run.
**Results pending.**

### How CMGMP lifts

Every CMGMP lift we rendered takes the same route, read by our formation
recognizer:

```text
{g} → {m_x, g} → {m_x, s, g} → {m_x, g_v, s_v} → {m_x, s_v} → {m_x, t}
```

The disk pushes the box against the riser and tips it into **our pivot
formation** {m_x, g_v, s_v}. The floor corner lets go and the box hangs on the
step corner, {m_x, s_v}. The disk keeps pushing and rolls the box a quarter
turn onto its +x face on the platform, {m_x, t}, with the disk still on the
face it pushed. Our planned route shares the pivot, then moves the disk round
the box's corner onto its top instead.

<video src="media/cmgmp/F1-lift-s0-00006_seed1.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**CMGMP, lift instance 6, seed 1 (23 s, real time).** Passes under the
full rule. The box drops off the pivot once for 0.15 s and regains it before
the roll.

<video src="media/cmgmp/F1-lift-s0-00021_seed3.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**CMGMP, lift instance 21, seed 3 (15 s).** Passes. The disk leaves the box
for a moment after the roll.

<video src="media/cmgmp/F1-lift-s0-00018_seed63.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**CMGMP, lift instance 18, seed 63 (15 s).** Passes, on the 64th seed: the
same route, found late.

### The redesign's first solutions: lowering, with a known issue

In the redesign's smoke test (three instances, a check of the code, not a
result) the search solved both lowering instances in 13 calls each. Each
solution is two calls: make the disk's contact on the box's +x face, then a
**release**: the disk pushes the box off the platform and lets it fall to the
floor. Both replays reproduce the logged calls exactly.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Known issue: the release throws the box

The release's push does not set the box down; it throws it. In instance 14
the box leaves at 1.46 m/s and lands 0.54 m past the predicted landing; in
instance 3, 0.19 m past. Both still end at rest inside the goal, so both
count. Releases also end in the same pose whatever formation they were asked
for. This is a property of the release's scripted push, not yet fixed.
:::

<video src="media/d23/v_linear_F1-lower-s0-00014.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Redesign, lower instance 14 (2 calls, 12 s).** make, then the release.
Watch the throw: the box lands well past the step.

<video src="media/d23/v_linear_F1-lower-s0-00003.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Redesign, lower instance 3 (2 calls, 9 s).** The same two calls; the box
lands 0.19 m past the prediction.

### Tonight's work: the lift's pivot

On elliptic contacts the lift stalled at its first hard step, the pivot
{m_x, g, s} ⇒ {m_x, g_v, s_v} (box flat against the riser tipping onto its
floor corner). The cause was a friction mismatch. The gate assumed the
simulator's disk–box friction, 0.99, and placed the disk 45 mm below the
middle of the box's face. The controller only uses 0.35, and from there it
could not tip the box: 0.01° over 680 samples. On pyramidal cones the same
pivot had passed only because the disk slipped up the face.

Two fixes, both decided by Aykut tonight:

1. **The gate uses the controller's friction, 0.35**, at the disk. The
   hard break that follows the pivot stays legal.
2. **The disk goes to the most robust placement.** The gate is re-checked
   exactly at several placements along the face (5 or 9; being finalized),
   and the one with the largest margin wins. This is an interim rule: in the
   long run a learned pivot skill chooses its own placement (three seeds are
   training now).

With both, lift instance 2's pivot passes into exactly {m_x, g_v, s_v}, with
the disk 44 mm *above* the face's middle, and the search went on to a release
onto the platform. A side finding: the exact gate passes at every disk height
on that face, but the controller succeeds only from about 10 mm below the
middle upward, so low on the face the gate is no test of what the controller
can do. Checking 9 placements costs about 3× per search node (13.5 → 40.5 s).

**Pending:** the redesign's full teacher run (lift and lower, elliptic
contacts), launching tonight; then the paired comparison with CMGMP and the
learned value's retraining.

## Earlier runs on pyramidal contacts (superseded) {#pyramidal}

::: {.callout-important}
## Superseded

Everything below was run on MuJoCo's pyramidal friction cones, under which
held boxes creep (see [above](#nov9)), and with the search as it was before
the redesign. These runs are not being continued; they are kept as the
record of what the old pipeline did.
:::

## The tie rule (`transfer_ties`)

The strict success test asks that an edit go from σ to σ′ with at most 40
"in-between" samples. In a **transfer** (one contact handing over to a
related one, such as the box's edge on the step corner becoming its face
on the platform), both contacts sit inside the recognizer's tolerance band
for a moment. Those samples are **ties**, and the current test counts them as
"in-between". The *proposed* rule, off by default and awaiting a decision,
reads a tied sample during a transfer as σ or σ′. The final dwell must still
be tie-free.

Clips that depend on the rule carry an orange **TIE RULE** badge. That
dependence is fragile. Both lift runs made the *same* final rolls, bit for
bit. On the cluster, the run without the rule rejected them and the run
with it accepted them. On this workstation's CPU, the re-runs of two of
those rolls pass even without the rule. Whether a roll needs the rule depends
on where one or two tied samples fall around the 40-sample limit. So the
badge says **TIE RULE (cluster)** when it rests on the cluster's verdicts.

## Lift: floor to platform

The box starts on the floor and has to end on the platform. The plan is the
same every time:

1. Λ_qs pushes the box against the riser and tips it onto the step corner,
   reaching the pivot.
2. The learned break skill lifts the box off the floor.
3. The learned roll skill sets it down on the platform.

::: {.callout-warning}
## What "on the platform" means here

The lift's goal test asks for the box to be flat, at platform height, and
partly over the platform (`cmg/teacher/scenes.py`, `goal_test`). Every
solved lift ends with the box **straddling the step edge**: its centre is
within about 1 cm of the corner, mostly over the floor side, and the disk
presses on its top. It probably would not stay there without the disk. This
is an open issue: a stricter goal, or a push-into-place (transport) edit at
the end.
:::

## The learned break skill against the quasi-static realizer

<video src="media/break_rl_vs_qs.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**break(g_v) from one start (lift instance 2, call 9; 9 s).** Top: the
learned skill Λ_RL lifts the floor corner off and holds the box on the step
corner. The strict test passes. Bottom: Λ_qs from the same state only tilts
the box further on its floor corner and never lets go of the floor. The
departure, dwell and sequence clauses fail. On the 84 break(g_v) states the
teacher's search reached, Λ_qs succeeds on none and the learned skill on
all 84. The bottom panel is a comparison run made for this video, not a
logged call.

The three short tasks the teacher run solves almost always (119 of 120).

<video src="media/sub_contact_00000.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Disk on the box's −x face (1 call, 9 s).** make(m_x) brings the disk

<video src="media/sub_flush_00001.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Box flush against the riser (2 calls, 17 s).** make(m_x), then make(s)
pushes the box against the riser.

<video src="media/sub_pivot_00003.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Pivot (2 calls, 17 s).** make(m_x), then one compound edit tips the box

## Open: lowering the box off the platform

The planner solves 0 of 40 lowering tasks. The CMGMP baseline lowered 19
of 25 (pyramidal contacts, 60 s per start; [now 24 of 25](#nov9) in 1,800 s
on elliptic contacts). The only way off the platform in our graph is a **knife-edge transfer**:
the box's bottom moves from the platform onto the step corner. It was tried in
the 11 instances whose box started 0.6–32.8 mm from the edge; farther away
nothing brings the box to the edge. Λ_qs fails it every time (52 of 52 calls).
These are the two ways it fails.

<video src="media/lower_knife_edge_fail.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Lower, instance 14, call 13 (9 s).** The disk slides across the box's
top while the box barely moves (0.4 mm). It never reaches the step corner,
so the dwell and sequence clauses fail.

<video src="media/lower_knife_edge_fall.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Lower, instance 3, call 7 (12 s) · DIVERGED.** Pushed from the side, the
box tips over the step edge and falls to the floor. On the cluster, 6 of the
52 such calls ended with the box down, all six inside the lowering goal, in 3
of the 40 instances (3, 14 and 27). The task's goal is met, but the edit
asked for a different formation, so the strict test rejects it. The redesign
decided on Nov 9 keeps such outcomes ([Search](../planar-build/search.qmd#redesign)). The re-run's
end pose matches the log within 7.3 mm, but a different clause fails first
(persistence here, dwell in the log), so the clip is labelled as diverged.

## Where these come from

- **Script:** `cmg/scripts/step4/videos/render.py` in `c-gnn` (commit
  `4b5194b`). `replay off|on` re-runs the logged calls, and `render` draws
  the clips. Its `manifest.json` lists every segment, whether its re-run
  matched the log, and the strict test's verdict with and without the tie
  rule.
- **Runs:** the teacher runs `t-full` (sub-goals and lowering), `t-lift-roll`
  (lift, tie rule off) and `t-lift-roll-ties` (lift, tie rule on). The tasks
  and numbers are on [Search and ranking](../planar-build/search.qmd).
